title: Teach the reader to name GitHub Actions cache branch scoping
summary: Add one short rule to the reader prompt (crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md): when a request touches CI caching or CI speed, the reading explains GitHub Actions cache branch scoping and states it in an acceptance criterion. Add a unit test in athena-context asserting the prompt names the constraint. The audience is the maintainer reviewing readings.

defaults_applied.how: New test added; cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
Criteria check the prompt text and a test that fails without it.
One prompt bullet and one test.
A test enforces the guidance remains in the prompt.
The criteria require the cache constraint to be named in a reading's criteria, checked via the prompt text.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The reading role's guidance means crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md, the READER_FRAME included via include_str!.
The test fixture is a unit test that checks the prompt text, in the style of the existing reader_checks_for_governance_files test; no model is run.
The reader budget (2000 tokens) is not raised. The addition is short, and the production reader's capability sections still fit.
No athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflow file changes. This request is about the prompt only.

acceptance_criteria.text: reader.md has a bullet saying that when a request touches CI caching or CI speed, the reading states how the GitHub Actions cache is scoped by branch and puts that constraint in an acceptance criterion.

The bullet states the scoping facts correctly: a run restores caches from its own branch (or PR merge ref), its base branch, and the default branch; it cannot restore caches created on sibling or unrelated branches; and caches saved by a feature branch are not visible to the default branch.

A new test in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs asserts that READER_FRAME.text contains the cache-scoping wording (CI cache, branch, base/default branch, criterion). Run `cargo test -p athena-context`; it passes, and it would fail if the bullet were removed.
The existing reader budget tests still pass, so the reader set stays within its 2000-token budget. Run `cargo test -p athena-context`. No budget constants change, and any added text is kept short.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Changing CI workflows or actual cache configuration
departures: Smaller than typical jobs: one prompt bullet and one test. The budget limit on reader.md adds a little risk.
